newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car sales fall for fourth month in a row.
newsitem.headline: French car sales fall for fourth month in a row.

text.p: French car sales fell 10.3 percent in April, the fourth consecutive monthly drop, as weak demand persisted more than six months after the end of a car-buying incentive programme, the French carmakers association CCFA said on Friday.
New car sales fell to 164,392 units last month from 183,244 a year earlier. On a same-day basis, they dropped 14.4 percent, as there were 22 working days last month, compared with 21 for April 1996.

"After a particularly bad first quarter -- car sales fell 26.5 percent, or 24.1 percent on a same-day basis -- April's results show slight improvement but are still at very low levels," the CCFA said in a statement.

French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen and Italy's Fiat registered the biggest sales declines. Peugeot and Citroen car sales fell 18.6 percent and Fiat sales fell 19.7 percent last month from inflated year-earlier levels.

Car sales surged in the first nine months of 1996 as the government gave rebates to car buyers turning in old clunkers. Demand has languished since the programme expired at the end of September 1996 in a worse-than-predicted backlash.

Renault SA fared relatively well in April, helped by the new Megane, Safrane and Espace models, and reported a 2.3 percent sales drop. Ford and Mercedes reported sales increases of four percent and 31.5 percent, respectively.
French carmakers took 54.4 percent of the market in April and had 55.3 percent in the January-April period.
